text: What is on the table in front of you right now? Describe it as if you will never see it again.
What did you eat today, and was any of it good?
Name three small things that went the way they were supposed to.
What would make tomorrow a little easier if you did it tonight?
Which sound do you notice most, once you stop to listen?
Write down the first thing you thought of this morning, before you were properly awake.
Who did you talk to today, and what was the one thing you remember them saying?
What is a small thing you are looking forward to?
What have you been putting off, and what is the smallest honest first step?
Describe someone who was kind to you this week. What did it cost them, and did they notice?
What are you carrying that you haven't told anyone about?
What did you want today that you didn't get? Was wanting it a mistake?
Where do you feel most like yourself, and when did you last go there?
What is something you believed five years ago that you no longer do?
What would you do this afternoon if no one needed anything from you?
Write about a smell that takes you somewhere. Where does it take you?
What part of today are you still turning over?
What do you hope is true about the person you are becoming?
What is one prayer, spoken or not, that you keep returning to? Say it plainly here.
Where did you notice grace today, in a person, a thing, or a pause?
Tell the story of the dream as far as you remember it, and leave the gaps as gaps.
If you could say one thing to a person you have lost touch with, what would it be?
Write to the version of you that will read this in ten years. What do you want them to remember about this week?
What do you owe someone that you have not paid? What would paying it look like?
What are you afraid is true? What would you do if it were?
When did you last forgive someone, and was it for them or for you?
What do you want your life to have been about, and how close is today to that?
What has your faith asked of you lately that you haven't wanted to give?
Write about a time you were certain and wrong. What did being wrong teach you?
What would you tell yourself at the lowest point of this year? What would you leave unsaid?
